title: Writing: text, headings and paragraphs
p: Good structure makes a document easier to write and easier to read. This guide covers headings, text styles and paragraph layout, with keyboard shortcuts for the things you will do most often.
Quiet.md supports nine heading levels. Two or three are usually enough; deeper levels are useful for long specifications and detailed outlines.
Here are a few examples:
Type one to nine # characters followed by a space. You can also use ⌘ ⌥ 1 through ⌘ ⌥ 9. The slash menu lists the first five levels; ⌘ ⌥ 0 turns a heading back into body text.
Headings appear automatically in the page outline. For a long document, write the outline first and then fill in each section.
Type 1. at the beginning of a heading to enable automatic numbering. Numbers follow the heading hierarchy and update when you insert or move a section.
Start with the problem you want to understand.
Numbering also appears in the outline.
Hover to the left of a heading and click its triangle to hide or show the section below it. Paragraphs and list items with children can fold too.
Folding changes what you see, not what is saved. Click the triangle again to fold this section.
Select some text to reveal the formatting toolbar, or use a shortcut.

img.caption: Select text to reveal the formatting toolbar

p: Styles can overlap: bold and underlined, or italic and crossed out. Markdown formatting is applied when you type the closing marker. Press ⌘ Z once to undo the conversion and keep the literal characters.

callout.p: ~text~, _italic_ and __bold__ need spaces or line boundaries around them. This keeps a name such as file_name from turning into formatting.

p: The toolbar's A control offers text colors and background highlights. Reusing a small set of colors helps readers understand what each one means.
Gray, red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple.
You can combine colors: needs attention or checked and complete. Press ⌘ ⌥ H to apply your last-used colors to another selection. Use the reset option in the color panel to remove them.
To color a whole paragraph, open its block menu and choose a background color. This paragraph uses light blue.
Adjacent paragraphs with the same background visually join into one area.
Select text and press ⌘ K to add a URL, such as the macOS website. With no selection, you can enter both the label and the URL.

ul.li: Typing an address beginning with https://, http:// or www., followed by a space, turns it into a link.
Hover over a link to edit it, remove it or copy its address.
Click a link to open it in your browser.
For links between notes, type @; see {{doc:organize}}.

p:
Enter starts a new paragraph. ⇧ Enter inserts a line break inside the current one.
This line belongs to the same paragraph as the one above.
Center text with ⌘ ⇧ E.
Align right with ⌘ ⇧ R.
Restore left alignment with ⌘ ⇧ L. These controls are also in the block menu.

Press Tab to make a paragraph a child of the one above it. Press ⇧ Tab to move it back out.
This is a child paragraph. It moves and folds with its parent.
Children can have children of their own.
At the start of a line, type a marker followed by a space unless noted otherwise.

td.p: Code block; Space or Enter completes it
Divider, as soon as you type the third dash

ul.li: ⌘ Z undoes an edit; ⌘ ⇧ Z or ⌘ Y redoes it. Continuous typing is grouped into a single undo step.
Copying within Quiet.md preserves styles, colors, tables and images.
Pasting from a web page or Feishu preserves supported document structure. Markdown text is converted on paste.
The bottom-right counter shows the word count of selected text.
